[[File:Paeonia officinalis MHNT.BOT.2015.34.59.jpg|thumb|''Paeonia officinalis'' - [[MHNT]]]]

'''''Paeonia officinalis''''', the '''common peony''',<ref>{{PLANTS|id=PAOF2|taxon=Paeonia officinalis|accessdate=30 January 2016}}</ref> or '''garden peony''',<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |accessdate=17 October 2014 }}</ref> is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] Paeoniaceae, [[native plant|native]] to mainly mountainous areas of Southern Europe and introduced in [[Central Europe|Central]] and [[Western Europe|Western]] Europe and North America.<ref name=IUCN>{{cite web |title=''Paeonia officinalis'' |url=https://www.iucnredlist.org/species/162001/103711428 |website=iucnredlist.org |date=14 February 2014 |publisher=[[IUCN]] |access-date=26 October 2020}}</ref>

''Paeonia officinalis'' was first used for medicinal purposes, then grown as an ornamental. Many selections are now used in horticulture, though the typical species is uncommon. ''Paeonia officinalis'' is still found wild in Europe.<ref name="Halda">{{cite book |last1=Halda |first1=Josef J. |last2=Waddick |first2=James W. |title=The Genus Paeonia |publisher=Timber Press |date=2004 |page=196 |isbn=978-0-88192-612-5 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=mDLASKInbjgC&pg=PA196}}</ref>

The [[cultivar]] 'Rubra Plena' (deep crimson double flowered) has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref>{{cite web |title=RHS Plant Selector - ''Paeonia officinalis'' 'Rubra Plena' |url=http://apps.rhs.org.uk/plantselector/plant?plantid=1372 |access-date=25 May 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190913090543/https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/details?plantid=1372 |archive-date=13 September 2019 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Description==
It is a [[herbaceous plant|herbaceous]] [[perennial plant|perennial]] growing to {{convert|60|-|70|cm|0|abbr=on}} tall and wide, with leaves divided into 9 leaflets, and bowl-shaped deep pink or deep red flowers, {{convert|10|-|13|cm|0|abbr=on}} in diameter, in late spring (May in the Northern Hemisphere).<ref name=RHSAZ>{{cite book |title=RHS A-Z encyclopedia of garden plants |year=2008 |publisher=Dorling Kindersley |location=United Kingdom |isbn=978-1405332965 |pages=1136}}</ref>

==Distribution==
The common peony is native to Europe in Spain, northern Portugal and southern France, Italy, Switzerland, western Romania and the [[Balkan Peninsula]] and possibly northern Greece (Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh 1998, Lupo Osti 2006, Aghababian 2011, GRIN 2014). It is widely cultivated elsewhere, but considered a native endemic of Europe.<ref name=IUCN></ref>

''fimbrata'', ''P. peregrina'' var. ''officinalis'', [[Form (botany)|f.]] ''officinalis'', ''P. porrigens'', ''P. promiscua'', ''P. pubens'', ''P. rubens'', ''P. sessiliflora'', ''P. splendens'', ''P. subternata'', ''P. versicolor''.{{citation needed|date=October 2020}}

=== Genetics ===
The common peony is an [[allotetraploid]] with two double sets of chromosomes from different parents (2n+2m=20), so it is a hybrid or [[nothospecies]]. One of the parents is most likely ''[[Paeonia peregrina]]''. The other parent is one of the group of very closely related species, ''[[Paeonia parnassica]]'', ''P. arietina'' and ''P. humilis''. Both these parents are tetraploids themselves. ''P. officinalis'' has by far the most extensive range and is one of the more abundant species in the Mediterranean region.<ref>{{cite journal |first1=Diane |last1=Ferguson |first2=Tao |last2=Sang |year=2001 |title=Speciation through homoploid hybridization between allotetraploids in peonies (''Paeonia'') |journal=[[Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America]] |volume=98 |issue=7 |pages=3915–3919 |url=http://www.pnas.org/content/98/7/3915.full.pdf |access-date=30 April 2016 |doi=10.1073/pnas.061288698 |pmid=11259655 |pmc=31153 |bibcode=2001PNAS...98.3915F |doi-access=free}}</ref>
